comment: The brain wire, version 4: the one protocol between a brain's driver (Go: apps/locus/keeper/internal/brainwire, which cmd/cyfr-claude-code and cmd/cyfr-codex share) and its holder (Opus.Brain.Wire, Elixir), over a `run` session of the backends service, each way one JSON object per line. A line is at most `max_line_bytes` bytes, UTF-8, the object's members exactly those its message names in `fields` (each present) and `optional` (each present or absent), each of the type `types` names: `id` a non-empty string of at most `max_id_bytes` bytes; `string` any string; `count` a whole number from 0; `boolean`; `object` a JSON object; `ids` and `strings` arrays of ids and of strings; `content` an array of blocks, each one `blocks` shows; `tools` an array of tools, each `{name, description, parameters}` with a name of 1 to 128 bytes, a description string and parameters an object; a tool is carried, one every harness carries whole, when its description is at most `tools.max_description` UTF-16 code units (as JavaScript counts a string: Claude Code keeps no more), its parameters name none of `tools.uncarried` among their `properties`, when an object, nor their `required`, when a list, (the stub's own answer members, which Claude Code's driver takes out of every call's arguments), and it is at most `tools.max_stub_argument` bytes as the stub's argument, the tool as `{description, inputSchema, name}` in the driver's JSON (Go's, its strings' U+2028 and U+2029 escaped, its parameters the line's own bytes); a line may carry a tool that is not carried, which a driver refuses, and the holder hands an outside server's tool only when it is carried, with the list's carried tools at most `tools.max_tools_bytes` bytes as those arguments, each a JSON string in one array, so that what a line carries beside them fits. `tools.cases` and `tools.lists` give tools and lists at each bound, each tool its `tool` with its description, when `description` names `[text, times]`, that text so many times, and with `parameters.description` of `pad` letters y when it names one, each with the bytes it takes and whether it is carried or fits; `config` an object of the members `config` names, each of its type; `counts` an object of exactly the four `counts` names, each a count; `model_counts` an array of `{model, counts}`, the model an id and the counts `counts`; `models` an array of `{id, name, efforts}`, the id an id, the name a string and the efforts `strings`, those that model takes; `choices` an array of `{id, name}`, both strings, the id an id; `phase` one of `phases`; `error_type` one of `error_types`; `accounting` one of `accountings`; `stop` one of `stops`; `account` one of `accounts`; `signed_in` and `signed_out` that word alone. A list holds at most `max_list` entries. A line that does not read so, names a `t` the other side does not take, or is past a bound, ends the session: `refuse` gives such lines, each with its reason, and `read` gives lines that read, each with what it reads as. Commands go from the holder to the driver, events from the driver to the holder. The driver's first line is `hello`, naming the version and its `boot`, fresh for each driver process; the holder ends a session whose `hello` names another version, so a driver that does not know a member of this one is never written to. A `start`'s `config.access` names one of the access choices the driver lists in a `models` answer's `access`, each `{id, name}`, the name the words a person reads: the driver lists only a choice it can honour in the box, starts and resumes its harness with the native settings of the one named (absent, its first listed), and a start naming one it does not list ends the driver before anything starts. A choice is the harness's own setting and no boundary of CYFR's: the driver answers each permission question of its harness with allow, and no choice restricts CYFR's tools, which CYFR's gate decides. A delivery (`work`, `post`, `answer`) names the id the holder stored it under; `models` and `forget` an id the holder chose. The driver answers each command once: `start` with `started` or `gone`, `work`, `post` and `answer` with `accepted` once the harness's input took it or `refused` when it was not written, `models` with `models` or `refused` (a listing the driver started a harness for is refused while that harness's account reads signed out, and when its account could not be read, as that), `forget` with `forgot` or `refused`; the holder writes the next command only once the last is answered. `account` is what the driver read positively in its harness's own account answer for that very event: `signed_out` only the one shape that harness answers with no sign-in, `signed_in` only a sign-in, key or other provider the answer names, and no member for an answer it does not know, one it could not read or none read. A `started` may carry either, a `models` only `signed_in` and a `refused` only `signed_out`; nothing else says anything of the account, an `authentication` error, an `idle` and an event without the member included. `signed_in` says that a sign-in or key is there, never that its provider still takes it. `accepted` says the harness's pipe took the command and is not durable delivery: a post Codex accepted and then lost with its process can be missing from its transcript. `forgot` says the session's transcript and whatever holds its content are gone, each removed or proved absent; a diagnostic line of the harness's that names only the removed session's id may remain. A `start`'s `tools` are the tools a new native session starts with, for a harness whose session keeps the tools it started with for its life (Codex: a resume keeps the thread's own and a `work` changes none of them, so a tool a later work adds is not one the harness can call, and an ask of one the work lacks is still the holder's to refuse); a harness that takes each work's tools (Claude Code) takes them from the `work` and none from the start. Every event of a native turn (`text`, `said`, `own`, `ask`, `usage`, `idle`, `error`) names the `gen` its session was started with and, when the driver knows it, the `work` of the command whose line started that native turn; a native turn no command started (a background command's end) names none, and every one of those events may come so. `native` names those events: the program's own lines, which the driver writes only when its harness wrote one; the rest are the driver's own. `usage` names a native `result` (Claude Code: each result's own identity, which gives no order, so nothing compares two of them; its counts the result's alone) or a cumulative `total` per native thread (Codex: the thread's id, its one entry in `models` the thread's counts so far across every model it ran, under the model it runs now; totals are compared by native thread across model changes and boots, the model a total names never makes a baseline of its own, and a total below the last is a reset; a resume may repeat the last total with no `work`, which against an unchanged baseline adds no spend, and an increase no work can be given stays unattributed), exactly one of the two, and its `accounting`: `complete`, every model's counts the harness reports for it, side requests included, each counted once, in `models`; `partial`, the models whose counts read, some did not, or (Codex) every total of the session from the first line of a thread not the session's (a sub-agent's, which the driver does not pass on) or the session's own call of a sub-agent, since whether a thread's total holds its sub-agents' counts is not established, and (Codex) a resumed session's first usable total, one that carries counts, which may end a stretch a sub-agent worked in whose total's event never committed, since the driver keeps nothing across processes; `unavailable`, the harness reported none, and `models` is absent, never zeros. `models` is present exactly when the accounting is not `unavailable`. A `post`'s input to the harness carries a uuid derived from the post's id (Claude Code: its user line's `uuid`; Codex: its `clientUserMessageId`), so a result or a native turn naming the uuid names the post: the uuid is the first 16 bytes of the SHA-256 of `uuid.prefix` followed by the id, with the version nibble set to 4 and the variant bits to 10, written in lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 form; `uuid.cases` gives ids and their uuids. A `start` that resumes names in `pending` the posts whose delivery is not known, and `started.held` names those of them the session's transcript holds: delivery evidence and no more, since a post in the transcript may never have been answered; a pending post it leaves out is not established, never proved absent. A resume replays nothing but, for Codex, the thread's last total, and goes on with nothing by itself. There is no interrupt: Stop closes the session.
